welcome: Welcome, Nature Guide! Pick a trail and let us look closely.
forest-intro: Forest Finds! Look carefully and tap the treasure I name.
find-maple-leaf: Can you find the maple leaf?
find-river-stone: Can you find the smooth river stone?
birds-intro: Bird Listening! Hear the call, then choose the bird who made it.
listen-chickadee: Listen closely. Which bird made that call?
listen-robin: A new forest song! Which bird made that call?
listen-woodpecker: Listen for the forest drummer. Which bird made that sound?
tracks-intro: Track Finder! Trace each trail, then choose the animal who left it.
trace-rabbit: Start at the glowing print and trace the rabbit trail.
trace-deer: Start at the glowing print and trace the deer trail.
trace-raccoon: Start at the glowing print and trace the raccoon trail.
trace-ready: Trail complete! Who left these tracks?
praise: Wonderful noticing! Into your nature journal it goes.
trace-again: Stay close to the trail and keep going.
forest-complete: Forest Finds complete! Your journal has three new treasures.
birds-complete: Bird Listening complete! Your journal is full of forest songs.
tracks-complete: Track Finder complete! You followed every clue.
journal-intro: Here is your nature journal. Tap any discovery to hear its story.
journal-empty: Your journal is waiting for discoveries. Choose a trail to begin.
all-complete: You found every discovery! You are an official Local Nature Guide.
fact-pinecone: Pinecones hold and protect the seeds of pine trees.
fact-maple-leaf: A maple leaf has pointed lobes spreading out from one stem.
fact-river-stone: Moving water tumbles stones and slowly smooths their edges.
fact-chickadee: A chickadee can sing its own name: chick-a-dee-dee-dee.
fact-robin: Robins sing bright, whistled phrases from branches and lawns.
fact-woodpecker: Woodpeckers drum on wood to send a message through the forest.
fact-rabbit: A rabbit usually leaves its long hind prints ahead of its smaller front prints.
fact-deer: A deer track shows two pointed hoof marks, often shaped like a small heart.
fact-raccoon: Raccoon tracks have five long toes that look a little like tiny hands.
